# File format of the output files generated by the `export_data.R` script

## Introduction

This document describes the file format of the output files generated by the `export_data.R` script.

The script exports these files for each normalization method it is given (`--norm_method`, one or
more, comma-separated, or `auto`: the best one):

1. Concentration table
2. Normalized data
3. Normalized data with blank substraction
4. Processing history

### Injections and their order (columns)

The study samples are always in the tables; the QCs, blanks and calibration standards are in them
unless left out (app: *Keep in the tables*; script: `--keep_qc`, `--keep_blank`, `--keep_cal`,
`TRUE` by default). The blank-subtracted table never has the blanks.

The columns are ordered:

| Options | Order of the columns |
| ------- | -------------------- |
| Group per injection type (default) | by injection type, in the chosen order (default: QCs, the study sample groups, blanks, calibration standards), then by batch and injection order |
| Group per batch | by batch, then by injection order |
| Both | by batch, then by injection type, then by injection order |
| Neither | by injection order |

In the app, the order of the injection types is set by dragging the groups (each study sample group
on its own); script: `--group_by_type`, `--group_by_batch` and `--group_order` (a JSON array of
`QC`, `Blank`, `CalCurve` and `grp:<Class>`; `Samples` stands for the study sample groups not named).
The batch is the batch of the measurement, also when all batches were processed together (one batch
mode: the `Given Batch ID`).

### Common features of the table files

In all of those files, these are common.

* File format : `xlsx`
* Decimal point : Use point `"."` as the decimal point.
* Concentrations and peak areas have at most 3 decimals, retention times 2 and m/z values 5.
  Numbers are stored as numbers, also in the feature information (missing values that MS-DIAL
  writes as `null` are left empty).
* If any outlier samples are detected, they are not included in the tables.
* The table structure is as below, which is almost identical to the input file described in `standard_format_input_file.md`.

| Lines        |      1st     | 2nd column section |
| ------------ | ------------ | ------------------ |
| 1-(x)        |    *empty*   |     Sample info    |
| (x+1) onward | Feature info |    numeric data    |

#### First (x) lines of the 2nd column section for sample information

In one batch mode, the first 5 lines are `Class`, `File type`, `Injection order`, `Batch ID` and `Given Batch ID`.
`Given Batch ID` is a copy of `Batch ID` from the input file.
`Batch ID` is set to `all`.

In multi batch mode, the first 4 lines are `Class`, `File type`, `Injection order` and `Batch ID`.
`Batch ID` is a copy of `Batch ID` from the input file.

The `Class`, `File type` and `Injection order` lines contain basically copied data from the input file.

#### Starting from the (x+1)th line

* The (x+1)th line is the header line.
* Each line is for one feature/chemical except the header line.
* The 1st column section contains feature information.
* The 2nd column section includes all numeric data.

The feature information column section (1st section) includes the same columns as the input file.

`Alignment ID`,
`Average Rt(min)` and
`Average Mz`.

## Concentration table

### File name

* `(source file name).(normalization method).conc.xlsx`

### Contents

The calibratied concentration values of chemicals (i.e. targeted `Quant`features) in the study
samples, and the `QC`, `Blank` and `Standard` (calibration) samples that are kept, in the order
described above. `IS` features are not included in this table.
The concentrations of the calibration samples are back-calculated from their curves, with the same
LOD/LLOQ rules. The concentrations of the `Blank` samples are computed from their normalized data **without** blank
subtraction (row `Blank subtracted`: `Not subtracted`), with the calibration of their batch and the
same LOD/LLOQ rules, so that they show the level of each chemical in the blanks.

Values replaced by the LOD/LLOQ rules are coloured (in all sheets): red for LLOQ/4 (signal below the
LOD signal), yellow for LLOQ/2 (signal from the LOD signal to below the mean signal of the LLOQ level)
and blue for the LLOQ (signal at or above it, concentration below the LLOQ); light olive for values above
the ULOQ but within a curve that was not cut at it, olive for values above the highest calibration level
of the curve (extrapolated). The last sheet, `Legend`, explains the colours.

The chemical columns of each batch sheet include `Notes`: the notes on each calibration curve in full
(e.g. a curve kept although not valid, a batch using the global curve, the levels above the ULOQ); the
app and the reports show them as icons.

When the processing option **Replace values below the LOD/LLOQ** is unticked (`--impute_llox=FALSE`),
these values are not replaced: their cells hold the text `n.d.` (not detected, below the LOD; red) or
`n.q.` (not quantified, between the LOD and the LLOQ; yellow) instead of a number. All other cells stay
numbers. Values set to the LLOQ (signal at or above the LLOQ level) are kept as before (blue).

### One batch mode

When there is only one batch, the file has just one spreadsheet. Its curves are fitted on all
samples, i.e. they are the global curves: the `Calibration` row and column say `Global`, and the
row `Blank subtracted` says `Average of all blanks`.

The feature information column section (1st section) includes additional columns for the concentration data on top of the columns common to all the tables.

`Chemical`,
`DF%` (detection frequency),
`Samples (d/n)` (detected/total),
`Concentration` (unit),
`LOD`,
`LLOQ`,
`Min Conc.`,
`Max Conc.`,
`Avg. Conc.`,
`Median Conc.`,
`R2`,
`Model`,
`Equation`,
`N of points`,
`Target IS`,
`Target IS (Rt)`,
`Slope`

### Multi batch mode

When there are multiple batches, the file has multiple spreadsheets.
The first sheet is `Full`, which contains all batches.
The rest of the sheets have the data of each batch.

#### `Full` sheet

The `Full` sheet contains all batches.

The feature information column section (1st section) includes additional columns as below.

`Chemical`,
`DF%`,
`Samples (d/n)` (detected/total),
`Concentration` (unit),
`Avg. Conc.` and `Median Conc.` (over the measured values of all batches together)

The minimum, maximum, average and median concentrations (here and per batch) are those of the
study samples only (no QCs), from the measured values at or above the LLOQ: values replaced by the
LOD/LLOQ rules are left out.

#### Sheets for each batch

Each sheet has the data of one batch.
The feature information column section (1st section) follows the same format as one batch mode tables.

## Normalized data tables

### File name

* `(source file name).(normalization method).norm.xlsx`

### Contents

Normalized values of all features except internal standards in the study samples and the `QC`,
`Blank` and `Standard` samples that are kept, in the order described above.

### Feature information columns

The feature information column section (1st section) is a reordered copy of the same section in the input file.

For the `closest` RT normalized data only, additionally `Target IS` and `Target IS (Rt)` columns are included.
The `Target IS` column contains the name of the closest internal standard feature that was used for normalization.
The `Target IS (Rt)` column contains the retention time of the closest internal standard feature.

## Normalized and blank subtracted data tables

### File name

* `(source file name).(normalization method).norm_blk.xlsx`

### Contents

Normalized and blank subtracted values of all features except internal standards in the study
samples and the `QC` and `Standard` samples that are kept, in the order described above. The
`Blank` samples are never included in this table.

### Feature information columns

The feature information column section (1st section) is a reordered copy of the same section in the input file.

For the `closest` RT normalized data only, additionally `Target IS` and `Target IS (Rt)` columns are included.
The `Target IS` column contains the name of the closest internal standard feature that was used for normalization.
The `Target IS (Rt)` column contains the retention time of the closest internal standard feature.

## Processing history

### File name

* `(source file name).(normalization method).history.xlsx`

### Contents

What happened to each feature and each sample during the processing, made from the event log of
`process.R` (`to_report[["events"]]`). Its sheets:

* `Feature history`: one row per feature of the input file, also those removed on the way (failed
  internal standards, blank filter, QC RSD% filter). After the feature information (`Feature`,
  `Alignment ID`, `Type`, `RT [min]`, `m/z`) its `Status` (where it ended, e.g. `Quantified`,
  `Kept`, `Removed (blank filter)`), then a column per processing step in the order of the
  processing: `Failed IS check`, `Normalized by`, `Blank filter`, `QC RSD% filter`, one
  `Calibration, batch N` per batch (the curve used, or why the feature was not quantified), and
  `Notes` (e.g. levels above the linear range). A cell tells what the step did (`Passed`,
  `Removed: <why>`, `Not applied`, ...); it is empty where the step does not concern the feature,
  or the feature was removed before.
* `Sample history`: one row per sample of the input file: `Sample`, `Sample type`, `Class`, `Batch`,
  `Injection order`, `Status` (`Kept` / `Removed (outlier)`), `vIS pre-normalization`,
  `Outlier check`, `IS zeros replaced` (how many zeros of the internal standards were replaced
  for the normalization, and by what), `Blank subtraction` (which blank mean), and one
  `Calibration (<version>)` per data version (the calibration of the sample's batch).
* `Events`: everything the processing logged that concerns this data version or all of them, one
  row per feature, sample or batch: `Step`, `Applies to` (feature, sample, batch or run), `Name`,
  `ID`, `Batch`, `Kind` (`removed`, `fallback`: the data did not allow the usual way, `changed`: a
  value replaced, `note`), `Event` and `Detail`.
* `Legend`: the explanation of the sheets.

As for the other tables, each sheet (but the legend) is also saved as a CSV file:
`(source file name).(normalization method).history.(sheet).csv`.
